verdict.rationale: Muse documents that once a user sets a goal or task, it 'continues to work on a schedule and in response to relevant events.' That work is tracked in a Goals tab and continues after the app is closed, so the product itself runs ongoing, recurring work. However, the evidence never shows user-defined recurrence controls (cron-like intervals, specific times, editing a schedule), and the scheduling appears to be driven by the agent rather than explicitly configured by the user. missing for 10: explicit user-configurable recurring schedules (frequency/time settings), schedule management and editing docs, independent or hands-on corroboration of recurring execution.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

citations.quote: Once you've set a goal or a task, Muse continues to work on a schedule and in response to relevant events, taking the next step and following up
The Goals tab is where Muse keeps track of all this for you, and you can interact directly there or talk to it about these tasks in chat.
Muse keeps things moving after you close the app. It monitors, follows up, and sends a notification when something needs your attention
